cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: How does a hardware accelerator turn two matrices into sixteen correct answers?

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: Let us follow one answer: eighty.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: We are Aman Soni, Mayank Sharma, and Ankit Kumar Pandey.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: Our project is a four-by-four systolic array matrix multiplication accelerator in Verilog.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: Matrix multiplication is a core operation in AI.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: Our idea is to reuse operands as they move through sixteen processing elements,

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: with several elements computing in parallel.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: I am Aman, and I designed the processing element, our basic multiply-accumulate unit.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: For our chosen output, the first row of A meets the first column of B.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: The calculation is one times sixteen, plus two times twelve, plus three times eight, plus four times four:

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: eighty.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: Each element multiplies signed eight-bit inputs and adds the product to a thirty-two-bit accumulator.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: It updates only when both operands are valid.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: I also implemented reset, accumulator clear, and registered data forwarding.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: The unit testbench checks ten cases, including negative arithmetic and invalid inputs.

cues.speaker: Aman Soni
cues.text: Mayank will show how these elements work together.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: I am Mayank, and I connected the sixteen processing elements into a four-by-four array.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: A values travel to the right, while B values travel down.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Each element keeps its own partial sum, so each eventually produces one output matrix entry.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: This is output-stationary dataflow.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Our top-left element builds eighty,

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: while other elements calculate their outputs as the data wave reaches them.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Forwarding lets neighbouring elements reuse operands.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: The important challenge is timing: matching operands must reach each element together.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: I added internal input delays of zero, one, two, and three cycles across the rows and columns.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Valid signals follow the same delays.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: I also built a cycle-by-cycle scoreboard covering one hundred and five matrices, input gaps,

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: and reset recovery.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Ankit will show how the controller runs the complete operation.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: I am Ankit Kumar Pandey.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: I implemented the controller, top-level integration, and system verification.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: An external start pulse begins the operation.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: The controller clears previous sums, feeds four sets of matrix operands,

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: and allows eight drain cycles for pipeline propagation and result capture.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: Busy indicates that computation is active.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: When the output is captured, done pulses for one cycle, and the result remains available.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: The documented controller sequence spans fourteen clock cycles.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: I also created a Python reference model with forty directed and random vectors.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: Those are software reference checks; the RTL is checked by the Verilog testbenches.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: Here is the complete system testbench.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: It compares all sixteen outputs against independently calculated expected values.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: Test two uses the matrices we started with.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: Its first expected output is eighty.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: The documented run shows this test passing, followed by all nine system tests passing.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: The tests include identity and zero matrices, signed extremes, consecutive operations,

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: reset during computation, and output stability.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: In the report waveform, start begins the transaction, busy stays high during processing,

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: and done marks the captured result.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: The first result word is eighty, completing our example.

cues.speaker: Ankit Kumar Pandey
cues.text: The recorded PE and array runs also show ten unit tests and one hundred and five matrix cases passing.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: We followed eighty from four products to a checked matrix output.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: The same structure computes all sixteen results.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Our Phase One deliverable is a Verilog RTL prototype with simulation verification.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Next, we plan memory integration, larger matrices through tiling,

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: and FPGA deployment with resource and power measurements.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Our code, tests, and report are on GitHub.

cues.speaker: Mayank Sharma
cues.text: Thank you.
